title: The NFL's decision to put Terrion Arnold on paid administrative leave via placement on the commissioner's exempt list comes after he was arrested in Tampa and faces felony charges related to a kidnapping and robbery in February. He has denied the allegations through his representatives. A player on the exempt list is paid his salary but may not practice or attend games. The personal conduct policy says that "upon request and with the club’s permission he may be present at the club’s facility on a reasonable basis for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation, and other permitted non-football activities." Arnold and the NFLPA have three days to appeal once he's notified of his placement on the exempt list. The league says Arnold will be placed on the list once his contract is filed with the league.
